newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives to move key by-election writ soon.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives to move key by-election writ soon.

text.p: The ruling Conservative Party will fire the starting gun for a key by-election within the next month, party chairman Brian Mawhinney indicated on Thursday.
He told a press conference called by the party: "We will move the writ for the Wirral South by-election within the normal parliamentary conventions."
Under normal conventions, the writ for a by-election must be moved within three months of the death or resignation of a sitting member. The election then takes place some three weeks later.
Barry Porter, the Conservative MP for Wirral South in north-west England, died on November 3, and February 3 is therefore the conventional cut-off date for the writ to be moved.

There has been speculation that the Conservatives, fearing a further deterioration in their parliamentary position if they lost Wirral South, would simply refuse to call the by-election. Porter had a 8,183 vote majority at the 1992 general election.
Prime Minister John Major lost his overall majority in parliament last month when Labour won a by-election in Barnsley, northern England.
But Mawhinney said: "We will move the writ and I expect to win the seat." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
